headline: Simulations link Ca2+ and lipid binding to conformational selection in proteins
label: Ion Identity In Biomolecular Dynamics
summary: Microsecond and coarse-grained simulations now resolve how Ca2+ and membrane contacts shape protein conformational states.
synthesis: The dominant thread is how bound ions and membrane contacts are treated as determinants of protein structure in molecular simulation. In the antifreeze protein MaIBP_RIV, all-atom MD shows Ca2+ stabilising the flatness of the ice-binding site and ordering ice-like hydration on primary prism and basal planes. For Sorcin, microsecond all-atom MD on Anton 3 (~90 μs) indicates that Ca2+ loss drives inactivation, consistent with a coordination-biased conformational selection mechanism. Coarse-grained millisecond simulations of non-visual arrestins show that the C-tail governs isoform-specific local and global dynamics in aqueous and membrane environments. TRPV6 mapping with CG-MD, SILCS and docking locates cholesterol-binding regions across open and closed states, compared with cryo-EM sterol data. What is new is the explicit treatment of ion identity, coordination and membrane context as drivers of conformational behaviour rather than a uniform background.
